title.zh: 卷228 列傳十五 额尔德尼 达海 尼堪 库尔緾 英俄尔岱 满达尔汉 明安达礼
title.en: Volume 228 Biographies 15: E Er De Ni, Da Hai, Ni Kan, Ku Er Chan, Ying E Er Dai, Man Daerhan, Ming Andali
title.raw: 卷228 列傳十五 额尔德尼 达海 尼堪 库尔緾 英俄尔岱 满达尔汉 明安达礼

sentences.zh: 庫爾纏<sub>弟庫拜</sub>英俄爾岱滿達爾漢<sub>弟馬福塔</sub>明安達禮}}額爾德尼，納喇氏，世居都英額。

translations.literal: Ku'erchan (younger brother Kubai), Ying'e'erdai, Mandarhan (younger brother Mafuta), Ming'andali}} E Erdeni, of the Nara clan, whose family had long resided at Duying'e.
translations.idiomatic: This chapter treats Ku'erchan, Ying'e'erdai, Mandarhan, Ming'andali, and others. E Erdeni, of the Nara clan, came from a family long established at Duying'e.

sentences.zh: 少明敏，兼通蒙古、漢文。

translations.literal: From youth he was bright and keen, and was versed in both Mongol and Chinese writing.
translations.idiomatic: He was clever from boyhood and fluent in both Mongol and Chinese.

sentences.zh: 太祖時來歸，隸正黃旗滿洲。

translations.literal: In the time of Taizu he came over in submission and was enrolled in the Manchu Plain Yellow Banner.
translations.idiomatic: During the reign of Taizu he submitted and was assigned to the Manchu Plain Yellow Banner.

sentences.zh: 從伐蒙古諸部，能因其土俗、語言、文字宣示意旨，招納降附。

translations.literal: He followed campaigns against the Mongol tribes and, drawing on their local customs, language, and script, could proclaim the imperial will and win over those who surrendered.
translations.idiomatic: On campaigns against the Mongol tribes he could convey the throne's intent in their own customs, language, and writing and bring in those who submitted.

sentences.zh: 賜號『巴克什』。

translations.literal: He was granted the title "Bakshi."
translations.idiomatic: The court bestowed on him the title Bakshi.

sentences.zh: 滿洲初起時，猶用蒙古文字，兩國語言異，必迻譯而成文，國人以為不便。

translations.literal: When the Manchu state was first rising it still used the Mongol script; the two peoples spoke different languages, so documents had to be translated into writing, which the people found inconvenient.
translations.idiomatic: In the early Manchu rise the state still relied on Mongol writing; because the languages differed, every document had to be translated, which countrymen found cumbersome.

sentences.zh: 太祖起兵之十六年，歲己亥二月辛亥朔，召巴克什額爾德尼、扎爾固齊、噶蓋使製國書。

translations.literal: In the sixteenth year after Taizu raised his army, in the second month of the jihai year on the day xinhai, the first of the month, he summoned Bakshi E Erdeni, Jarguci, and Gai to make the national script.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixteenth year of Taizu's uprising, on the first day of the second month of jihai (1599), he called Bakshi E Erdeni, Jarguci, and Gai to create a national script.

sentences.zh: 額爾德尼、噶蓋辭以夙習蒙古文字，未易更制。

translations.literal: E Erdeni and Gai declined, saying they had long been accustomed to the Mongol script and that a change would not be easy.
translations.idiomatic: E Erdeni and Gai pleaded that long habit in the Mongol script made reform difficult.

sentences.zh: 上曰：『漢人誦漢文，未習漢字者皆知之；

translations.literal: The emperor said: "When Chinese recite Chinese text, even those who have not studied Chinese characters understand it;
translations.idiomatic: The emperor replied: "When Chinese read Chinese aloud, even those who never learned the characters understand;"

sentences.zh: 蒙古人誦蒙古文，未習蒙古字者皆知之。

translations.literal: When Mongols recite Mongol text, even those who have not studied Mongol characters understand it.
translations.idiomatic: when Mongols read Mongol aloud, even the illiterate understand."

sentences.zh: 我國語必譯為蒙古語，始成文可誦；

translations.literal: Our national language must be rendered in Mongol before it becomes a text that can be recited;
translations.idiomatic: Our tongue must be turned into Mongol before it becomes readable text;

sentences.zh: 則未習蒙古語者，不能知也。

translations.literal: then those who have not learned Mongol cannot understand.
translations.idiomatic: so anyone who has not learned Mongol cannot follow it."

sentences.zh: 奈何以我國語製字為難，而以習他國語為易耶？』

translations.literal: Why, then, treat making characters for our language as hard, and learning another people's language as easy?"
translations.idiomatic: Why call it hard to devise a script for our own speech, yet easy to master a foreign tongue?"

sentences.zh: 額爾德尼、噶蓋請更制之法，上曰：『是不難。

translations.literal: E Erdeni and Gai asked how to change the system. The emperor said: "That is not difficult.
translations.idiomatic: E Erdeni and Gai asked for a method of reform. The emperor said: "That is not difficult."

sentences.zh: 但以蒙古字協我國語音，聯屬為句，因文以見義可矣。』

translations.literal: Simply adapt Mongol letters to the sounds of our language, join them into sentences, and let the writing convey the meaning.
translations.idiomatic: Adapt Mongol letters to our phonology, link them into sentences, and let the script carry the sense."

sentences.zh: 於是製國書，行於國中。

translations.literal: Thereupon the national script was made and put into use throughout the state.
translations.idiomatic: The national script was then produced and circulated within the realm.

sentences.zh: 滿洲有文字自此始。

translations.literal: From this time Manchu writing began.
translations.idiomatic: Manchu writing dates from this moment.

sentences.zh: 天命三年，從伐明，取撫順，師還。

translations.literal: In the third year of Tianming he followed the campaign against Ming, took Fushun, and the army returned.
translations.idiomatic: In Tianming 3 he joined the attack on Ming, captured Fushun, and withdrew.

sentences.zh: 明總兵張承廕自廣寧率衆臨我師，后額爾德尼偕諸將還擊，斬承廕。

translations.literal: Ming regional commander Zhang Chengyin led troops from Guangning against our army; afterward E Erdeni with the generals turned back to strike, and beheaded Chengyin.
translations.idiomatic: When Ming commander Zhang Chengyin marched from Guangning against the army, E Erdeni and other generals counterattacked and killed him.

sentences.zh: 叙功，授副將。

translations.literal: For merit in the campaign he was appointed vice commander.
translations.idiomatic: For his service he was made vice commander.

sentences.zh: 太宗時，額爾德尼已前卒，嘗諭文館諸臣，歎為一代傑出。

translations.literal: In the time of Taizong, E Erdeni had already died earlier; the emperor once told the Literary Bureau that he was an outstanding man of his generation.
translations.idiomatic: By Taizong's reign E Erdeni was already dead; the emperor once told the Literary Bureau he had been a man of rare talent.

sentences.zh: 順治十一年，追諡文成。

translations.literal: In the eleventh year of Shunzhi he was posthumously given the temple name Wencheng.
translations.idiomatic: In Shunzhi 11 he received the posthumous name Wencheng.

sentences.zh: 子薩哈連，官至鑾儀衛冠軍，使賜姓赫舍里，改入大學士希福族中。

translations.literal: His son Sahalian rose to Champion of the Imperial Procession Guard; on a mission he was granted the surname Heseri and was transferred into the clan of Grand Secretary Xifu.
translations.idiomatic: His son Sahalian became Champion of the Imperial Procession Guard; on embassy he received the surname Heseri and was enrolled in Grand Secretary Xifu's clan.

sentences.zh: 噶蓋，伊爾根覺羅氏，世居呼納赫。

translations.literal: Gai, of the Irgen Gioro clan, whose family had long resided at Hunahe.
translations.idiomatic: Gai, of the Irgen Gioro clan, came from Hunahe.

sentences.zh: 後隸滿洲鑲黃旗。

translations.literal: Later he was enrolled in the Manchu Bordered Yellow Banner.
translations.idiomatic: He was later assigned to the Manchu Bordered Yellow Banner.

sentences.zh: 太祖以為扎爾固齊，位亞費英東。

translations.literal: Taizu made him a jarguci, ranking below Fei Yingdong.
translations.idiomatic: Taizu appointed him jarguci, second only to Fei Yingdong.

sentences.zh: 歲癸巳閏十一月，命與額亦都、安費揚古將千人攻納殷佛多和山寨，斬其酋搜穩寨克什。

translations.literal: In the intercalary eleventh month of guisi he was ordered with Eidu and Anfiyanggu to lead a thousand men against the Nain Foduhe mountain fort and beheaded its chief Suwensaikeashi.
translations.idiomatic: In the intercalary eleventh month of guisi he and Eidu and Anfiyanggu led a thousand men against the Nain Foduhe stockade and killed its chief Suwensaikeashi.

sentences.zh: 歲戊戌正月，命與台吉褚英、巴雅喇及費英東將千人伐安褚拉庫路，降屯寨二十餘。

translations.literal: In the first month of wuxu he was ordered with Taisun Cuying, Bayara, and Fei Yingdong to lead a thousand men against the Antuhalaku circuit and reduce more than twenty stockades.
translations.idiomatic: In the first month of wuxu he, Cuying, Bayara, and Fei Yingdong led a thousand men against Antuhalaku and took more than twenty forts.

sentences.zh: 歲己亥，受命製國書。

translations.literal: In the year jihai he was ordered to help make the national script.
translations.idiomatic: In jihai he was charged with creating the national script.

sentences.zh: 是年九月，命與費英東將二千人戍哈達。

translations.literal: In the ninth month of that year he was ordered with Fei Yingdong to garrison Hada with two thousand men.
translations.idiomatic: That September he and Fei Yingdong were sent to garrison Hada with two thousand troops.

sentences.zh: 哈達貝勒孟格布祿貳於明，將執二將。

translations.literal: Hada beile Menggebulu turned disloyal to Ming and was about to seize the two generals.
translations.idiomatic: Hada beile Menggebulu wavered toward Ming and planned to arrest the two commanders.

sentences.zh: 二將以告，太祖遂滅哈達，以孟格布祿歸。

translations.literal: The two generals reported this, and Taizu then destroyed Hada and brought Menggebulu back.
translations.idiomatic: They reported it; Taizu destroyed Hada and brought Menggebulu back.

sentences.zh: 孟格布祿有逆謀，噶蓋坐不覺察，併誅。

translations.literal: Menggebulu harbored treacherous designs; Gai was punished for failing to detect them and was executed with him.
translations.idiomatic: When Menggebulu plotted rebellion, Gai was condemned for not detecting it and was executed with him.

sentences.zh: 子武善。

translations.literal: His son was Wushan.
translations.idiomatic: He left a son, Wushan.

sentences.zh: 武善年十六，太祖念噶蓋舊勞，授牛錄額真。

translations.literal: When Wushan was sixteen, Taizu, mindful of Gai's old service, appointed him niru captain.
translations.idiomatic: At sixteen Wushan received a niru captaincy in remembrance of Gai's service.

sentences.zh: 天命九年，明將毛文龍遣兵入海島屯耕。

translations.literal: In the ninth year of Tianming the Ming general Mao Wenlong sent troops to island bases to farm.
translations.idiomatic: In Tianming 9 Mao Wenlong sent men to farm on offshore islands.

sentences.zh: 語詳冷格里傳。

translations.literal: The account is given in detail in the biography of Lenggeli.
translations.idiomatic: The fuller account appears in Lenggeli's biography.

sentences.zh: 文龍復遣兵三百登海岸掠，武善與滿？

translations.literal: Wenlong again sent three hundred men ashore to raid; Wushan and Manduli
translations.idiomatic: Wenlong again sent three hundred men to raid the coast; Wushan and Manduli

sentences.zh: ，太祖命武善與冷格里擊之，殲其都裡率兵追擊，斬裨將三，還所掠。

translations.literal: , and Taizu ordered Wushan and Lenggeli to attack them, annihilating the enemy; Manduli pursued, beheaded three deputy commanders, and recovered what had been looted.
translations.idiomatic: met them; Taizu then ordered Wushan and Lenggeli to strike, wiped out the raiders, and Manduli pursued, killing three lieutenant generals and recovering the plunder.

sentences.zh: 太宗即位，列十六大臣，佐鑲紅旗。

translations.literal: When Taizong acceded, Wushan was listed among the Sixteen Ministers and assisted the Bordered Red Banner.
translations.idiomatic: At Taizong's accession Wushan became one of the Sixteen Ministers for the Bordered Red Banner.

sentences.zh: 天聰八年，上遣諸將伐明，武善與阿山為後隊，遵上方略，設伏敗敵，授三等甲喇章京。

translations.literal: In the eighth year of Tiancong the emperor sent generals against Ming; Wushan and Ashan formed the rear guard, followed the emperor's plan, set an ambush, and defeated the enemy; he was made a third-rank jalan commander.
translations.idiomatic: In Tiancong 8, on the Ming campaign, Wushan and Ashan commanded the rear, set an ambush as directed, routed the enemy, and received third-rank jalan rank.

sentences.zh: 崇德元年，诇知明兵襲濱海鹺場，上命武善與吏部參政吉恩哈馳援，擊走明兵。

translations.literal: In the first year of Chongde, learning that Ming troops were raiding the coastal salt works, the emperor ordered Wushan and Board of Personnel Vice Commissioner Ji'enha to hurry to their aid and drive off the Ming force.
translations.idiomatic: In Chongde 1, when Ming troops struck the coastal salt fields, Wushan and Ji'enha were sent in relief and repulsed them.

sentences.zh: 三年正月，喀爾喀扎薩克圖窺歸化城，上自將御之，武善與吳巴海從。

translations.literal: In the first month of the third year, when Khalkha Zasaktu eyed Guihua City, the emperor led the army in person; Wushan followed with Wubahai.
translations.idiomatic: In the first month of year 3, as Khalkha Zasaktu threatened Guihua, the emperor marched in person and Wushan followed with Wubahai.

sentences.zh: 吳巴海？

translations.literal: Wubahai's
translations.idiomatic: Wubahai's

sentences.zh: 卒盜軍糈，武善坐徇隱，奪世職。

translations.literal: soldiers stole military grain; Wushan was punished for concealment and lost his hereditary office.
translations.idiomatic: troops stole army rations; Wushan was punished for covering it up and lost his hereditary rank.

sentences.zh: 八月，授工部參政。

translations.literal: In the eighth month he was appointed vice commissioner of the Board of Works.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth month he became vice commissioner of Works.

sentences.zh: 時蒙古、瓦爾喀諸部皆附，使至，每以武善典其事。

translations.literal: At that time the Mongol and Warka tribes had all submitted; whenever envoys arrived, Wushan was usually put in charge.
translations.idiomatic: As Mongol and Warka tribes submitted, Wushan was routinely placed over incoming embassies.

sentences.zh: 順治元年，卒。

translations.literal: In the first year of Shunzhi he died.
translations.idiomatic: He died in Shunzhi 1.

sentences.zh: 布善，武善弟。

translations.literal: Bushan was Wushan's younger brother.
translations.idiomatic: Bushan was Wushan's brother.

sentences.zh: 事太宗，授巴牙喇甲喇章京，兼牛錄額真。

translations.literal: Serving Taizong, he was made a bayara jalan commander and also niru captain.
translations.idiomatic: Under Taizong he received bayara jalan rank and a niru captaincy.

sentences.zh: 尋護巴牙喇纛章京，列議政大臣。

translations.literal: Soon he guarded the bayara banner commander and was listed among the Deliberative Ministers.
translations.idiomatic: He later guarded the bayara standard and sat among the Deliberative Ministers.

sentences.zh: 崇德五年，從伐明，攻錦州，擊敗杏山騎兵。

translations.literal: In the fifth year of Chongde he followed the campaign against Ming, attacked Jinzhou, and defeated the Xingshan cavalry.
translations.idiomatic: In Chongde 5 he joined the Ming campaign, besieged Jinzhou, and routed Xingshan's horsemen.

sentences.zh: 六年，復從伐明，攻松山，洪承疇以十三萬人赴援，布善先众力戰卻敵。

translations.literal: In the sixth year he again followed the Ming campaign and attacked Songshan; Hong Chengchou came with a relief force of 130,000; Bushan fought ahead of the host and drove the enemy back.
translations.idiomatic: In year 6 at Songshan, as Hong Chengchou advanced with 130,000 men, Bushan fought in the van and repulsed them.

sentences.zh: 上度明兵眾而餉不繼，必引去，命諸將比翼列營，直抵海濱。

translations.literal: The emperor judged that the Ming army was numerous but could not sustain supplies and would certainly withdraw; he ordered the generals to camp wing to wing and press straight to the seashore.
translations.idiomatic: Judging the Ming host too large to feed and sure to retreat, the emperor ordered generals to camp abreast and drive to the coast.

sentences.zh: 入夜，明兵果引去，諸將截擊，布善率兵窮追，斬獲無算。

translations.literal: At night the Ming army did withdraw; the generals intercepted them, and Bushan pursued to the end, killing and capturing without number.
translations.idiomatic: That night the Ming force withdrew; generals cut them off and Bushan pursued relentlessly, with countless kills and captures.

sentences.zh: 八年，復從伐明，攻克前、中前所。

translations.literal: In the eighth year he again followed the Ming campaign and captured Qian and Zhongqian stations.
translations.idiomatic: In year 8 he again joined the Ming campaign and took Qian and Zhongqian stations.

sentences.zh: 順治初，從入關，予牛錄章京世職。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Shunzhi he followed the entry into the pass and was granted the hereditary office of niru commander.
translations.idiomatic: At the founding of Shunzhi he entered the pass and received a hereditary niru command.

sentences.zh: 二年，從征江南，卒於軍。

translations.literal: In the second year he followed the Jiangnan campaign and died in the army.
translations.idiomatic: In year 2 he campaigned in Jiangnan and died on campaign.

sentences.zh: 誇札，布善子，襲職。

translations.literal: Kuazha, Bushan's son, inherited the office.
translations.idiomatic: Kuazha, Bushan's son, succeeded to the post.

sentences.zh: 遇恩詔，進二等阿達哈哈番。

translations.literal: On an amnesty edict he was promoted to second-rank adahafan.
translations.idiomatic: An amnesty edict raised him to second-rank adahafan.

sentences.zh: 十七年，授護軍參領，兼佐領。

translations.literal: In the seventeenth year he was appointed deputy commander of the Guard and also assistant captain.
translations.idiomatic: In year 17 he became Guard deputy commander and assistant captain.

sentences.zh: 康熙十三年，從定南將軍希爾根討耿精忠，圍撫州，屢破賊，賊棄城走。

translations.literal: In the thirteenth year of Kangxi he followed General Xiergen of Dingnan against Geng Jingzhong, besieged Fuzhou, repeatedly defeated the rebels, and the rebels abandoned the city and fled.
translations.idiomatic: In Kangxi 13 he followed Xiergen against Geng Jingzhong, besieged Fuzhou, repeatedly routed the rebels, and they fled the city.

sentences.zh: 四年，從大將軍安親王岳樂討吳三桂，其將夏國相屯萍鄉，依山結寨。

translations.literal: In the fourth year he followed Grand General Prince An Yuele against Wu Sangui; Wu's general Xia Guoxiang held Pingxiang and built stockades on the hills.
translations.idiomatic: In year 4 he followed Prince An Yuele against Wu Sangui; Xia Guoxiang held Pingxiang on the hills.

sentences.zh: 誇札率兵奮擊，大破之，國相等棄資械走。

translations.literal: Kuazha led troops in a fierce assault, routed them completely, and Guoxiang and others abandoned weapons and supplies and fled.
translations.idiomatic: Kuazha stormed the position, broke it utterly, and Guoxiang fled abandoning equipment.

sentences.zh: 十七年，遷護軍統領。

translations.literal: In the seventeenth year he was transferred to commander of the Guard.
translations.idiomatic: In year 17 he was made Guard commander.

sentences.zh: 十八年，擢鑲紅旗蒙古都統。

translations.literal: In the eighteenth year he was promoted to Mongol commander of the Bordered Red Banner.
translations.idiomatic: In year 18 he rose to Mongol commander of the Bordered Red Banner.

sentences.zh: 從安親王攻武岡，軍器輜重自水道進，賊截溪，誇札率兵馳擊，賊卻走​​。

translations.literal: Following Prince An in the attack on Wugang, arms and baggage advanced by water; rebels blocked the stream and Kuazha led troops in a rush attack, and the rebels withdrew.
translations.idiomatic: At Wugang, as supplies moved by river and rebels blocked the stream, Kuazha charged and drove them off.

sentences.zh: 綠旗兵屯溪岸，賊舟坌集逼屯，誇札自陸赴援，道險，？

translations.literal: Green Banner troops were encamped on the stream bank; rebel boats massed and pressed the camp; Kuazha came to aid by land; the road was perilous and
translations.idiomatic: Green troops held the bank while rebel boats crowded in; Kuazha marched overland to relieve them, but the path was treacherous and

sentences.zh: ，馬不能行，乃率兵步行。

translations.literal: , horses could not pass, so he led the troops on foot.
translations.idiomatic: so narrow that horses could not pass; he continued on foot.

sentences.zh: 賊據山梁，設鹿角，列火器以拒，誇札督兵直前，斬獲甚賊水陸皆潰。

translations.literal: The rebels held the ridge, set abatis, and lined up firearms to resist; Kuazha directed the troops straight forward; kills and captures were great and the rebels collapsed by land and water.
translations.idiomatic: Rebels on the ridge with abatis and muskets blocked him; Kuazha pressed forward, inflicted heavy losses, and broke them on land and water.

sentences.zh: 十九年，命將湖廣兵詣廣西，參贊大將軍簡親王喇布軍務，討叛將馬承廕，克武寧，進取像州，圍柳州，承廕降，進复慶遠。

translations.literal: In the nineteenth year he was ordered to lead Huguang troops to Guangxi, assist Grand General Prince Jian Labu, and campaign against the rebel Ma Chengguang; he took Wuning, advanced on Xiangzhou, besieged Liuzhou; Chengguang surrendered, and he recovered Qingyuan.
translations.idiomatic: In year 19 he led Huguang forces to Guangxi to assist Prince Jian Labu against Ma Chengguang, took Wuning and Xiangzhou, besieged Liuzhou until Chengguang surrendered, and recovered Qingyuan.

sentences.zh: 廣西平，還京。

translations.literal: When Guangxi was pacified he returned to the capital.
translations.idiomatic: After Guangxi was pacified he returned to Beijing.

sentences.zh: 二十一年，卒。

translations.literal: In the twenty-first year he died.
translations.idiomatic: He died in year 21.

translations.literal: For his
translations.idiomatic: For his

sentences.zh: 功，進一等阿達哈哈番。

translations.literal: merit he was promoted to first-rank adahafan.
translations.idiomatic: service he was posthumously raised to first-rank adahafan.

sentences.zh: 達海，先世居覺爾察，以地為氏。

translations.literal: Dahai: his ancestors resided at Jiorca and took the place as their clan name.
translations.idiomatic: Dahai's forebears lived at Jiorca and took the place as their surname.

sentences.zh: 祖博洛，太祖時來歸。

translations.literal: His grandfather Boluo came over in submission in the time of Taizu.
translations.idiomatic: Grandfather Boluo submitted in Taizu's day.

sentences.zh: 父艾密禪。

translations.literal: His father was Aimishan.
translations.idiomatic: His father was Aimishan.

sentences.zh: 旗制定，隸滿洲正藍旗。

translations.literal: When the banners were fixed he was enrolled in the Manchu Plain Blue Banner.
translations.idiomatic: When banners were organized he joined the Manchu Plain Blue Banner.

sentences.zh: 達海幼慧，九歲即通滿、漢文義。

translations.literal: Dahai was clever from childhood; at nine he already understood Manchu and Chinese.
translations.idiomatic: Dahai was precocious; at nine he grasped Manchu and Chinese.

sentences.zh: 弱冠，太祖召直左右，與明通使命，若蒙古、朝鮮聘問往還，皆使屬草；

translations.literal: At his coming of age Taizu summoned him to attend at his side; for missions with Ming, and for Mongol and Korean embassies going back and forth, he was always made to draft documents;
translations.idiomatic: At majority Taizu kept him at court; he drafted all correspondence with Ming, Mongolia, and Korea;

sentences.zh: 令於國中，有當兼用漢文者，皆使承命傳宣：悉稱太祖旨。

translations.literal: throughout the state, wherever Chinese writing had to be used together with the national script, he was ordered to proclaim the command—all styled as Taizu's decree.
translations.idiomatic: wherever Chinese was needed domestically, he issued proclamations in the emperor's name.

sentences.zh: 旋命譯明會典及素書、三略。

translations.literal: He was soon ordered to translate the Ming Collected Statutes, the Su Shu, and the Three Strategies.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon set to translate the Ming Collected Statutes, Su Shu, and Three Strategies.

sentences.zh: 太宗始置文館，命分兩直：達海及剛林、蘇開、顧爾馬渾、托布戚譯漢字書籍；

translations.literal: When Taizong first established the Literary Bureau he ordered two shifts: Dahai with Ganglin, Sukai, Guermahun, and Tobuci translated Chinese books;
translations.idiomatic: Taizong's new Literary Bureau split into two shifts: Dahai, Ganglin, Sukai, Guermahun, and Tobuci translated Chinese texts;

sentences.zh: 庫爾？

translations.literal: Ku'er
translations.idiomatic: Ku'erchan,

sentences.zh: 、吳巴什、查素喀、胡球、詹霸記註國政。

translations.literal: chan, Wubashi, Chasuka, Huqiu, and Zhanba recorded and annotated state affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Wubashi, Chasuka, Huqiu, and Zhanba recorded state affairs.

sentences.zh: 天聰三年，上伐明，既擊破滿桂等四總兵軍，遣達海齎書與明議和，明閉關拒勿納；

translations.literal: In the third year of Tiancong the emperor attacked Ming; after breaking the armies of the four regional commanders including Man Gui, he sent Dahai with a letter to negotiate peace with Ming; Ming closed the passes and refused to receive it;
translations.idiomatic: In Tiancong 3, after defeating Man Gui and three other Ming commanders, Dahai was sent to sue for peace; Ming shut the gates and refused the letter;

sentences.zh: 復命達海為書二通，一置德勝門外，一置安定門外，乃引師還。

translations.literal: he again ordered Dahai to write two letters, one placed outside Desheng Gate and one outside Anding Gate, and then withdrew the army.
translations.idiomatic: Dahai wrote two letters left at Desheng and Anding Gates, then withdrew.

sentences.zh: 四年，复伐明，至沙河驛，命達海以漢語諭降。

translations.literal: In the fourth year he again attacked Ming; reaching Shahe Post, he ordered Dahai to announce surrender in Chinese.
translations.idiomatic: In year 4, reaching Shahe Post, Dahai was ordered to call for surrender in Chinese.

sentences.zh: 克永平，命達海持黃旗登城，以漢語諭軍民，城中望見，皆羅跪呼「萬歲」。

translations.literal: When Yongping was taken he ordered Dahai to ascend the wall with a yellow banner and address soldiers and civilians in Chinese; seeing this within the city, all knelt and cried "Long live the emperor!"
translations.idiomatic: At Yongping's fall Dahai mounted the wall with a yellow banner and addressed the populace in Chinese; the city knelt and shouted "Long live!"

sentences.zh: 降將孟喬芳、楊文魁、楊聲遠從貝勒阿巴泰入見，命達海以漢語慰勞。

translations.literal: The surrendered generals Meng Qiaofang, Yang Wenkui, and Yang Shengyuan followed Prince Abatai to audience; Dahai was ordered to comfort them in Chinese.
translations.idiomatic: Surrendered generals Meng Qiaofang, Yang Wenkui, and Yang Shengyuan were received through Prince Abatai; Dahai comforted them in Chinese.

sentences.zh: 三屯營、漢兒莊既降，明兵襲三屯營。

translations.literal: Santunying and Han'erzhuang had already surrendered when Ming troops raided Santunying.
translations.idiomatic: After Santunying and Han'erzhuang submitted, Ming raided Santunying.

sentences.zh: 上慮漢兒莊复叛，命達海以漢語撫定之。

translations.literal: Fearing Han'erzhuang would rebel again, the emperor ordered Dahai to pacify it in Chinese.
translations.idiomatic: Fearing Han'erzhuang might revolt, the emperor sent Dahai to reassure it in Chinese.

sentences.zh: 是年，所譯書成，授游擊。

translations.literal: That year, when the translations were finished, he was appointed guerrilla commander.
translations.idiomatic: When the translations were completed that year he received guerrilla rank.

sentences.zh: 五年七月，賜號「巴克什」。

translations.literal: In the seventh month of the fifth year he was granted the title "Bakshi."
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh month of year 5 he received the title Bakshi.

sentences.zh: 九月，复伐明，破大凌河，命達海以漢語招總兵祖大壽。

translations.literal: In the ninth month he again attacked Ming, broke Dalinghe, and ordered Dahai to summon regional commander Zu Dashou in Chinese.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth month, after taking Dalinghe, Dahai was sent to summon Zu Dashou in Chinese.

sentences.zh: 上賜宴，復命傳諭慰勞。

translations.literal: The emperor gave a banquet and again ordered him to convey words of comfort.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor feasted him and again ordered comforting words delivered.

sentences.zh: 十二月，定朝儀。

translations.literal: In the twelfth month court ritual was fixed.
translations.idiomatic: Court ceremony was fixed in the twelfth month.

sentences.zh: 達海治國書，補額爾德尼、噶蓋所未備，增為十二字頭。

translations.literal: Dahai worked on the national script, supplementing what E Erdeni and Gai had left incomplete, and expanded it to twelve syllabic heads.
translations.idiomatic: Dahai refined the national script, completing E Erdeni and Gai's work and expanding it to twelve syllabic heads.

sentences.zh: 六年三月，太宗諭達海曰：「十二字頭無識別，上下字相同。

translations.literal: In the third month of the sixth year Taizong instructed Dahai: "The twelve heads lack distinction; upper and lower characters are the same.
translations.idiomatic: In the third month of year 6 Taizong told Dahai: "The twelve heads are indistinguishable; identical forms stand for different readings.

sentences.zh: 幼學習之，尋常言語，猶易通曉；

translations.literal: If learned in youth, ordinary speech is still easy to understand;
translations.idiomatic: In childhood study ordinary speech is still intelligible;

sentences.zh: 若人姓名及山川、土地，無文義可尋，必且舛誤。

translations.literal: but for personal names and for mountains, rivers, and lands, where no meaning can be inferred from the text, errors are inevitable.
translations.idiomatic: but personal names and place-names have no inferable sense and will surely be misread.

sentences.zh: 爾其審度字旁加圈點，使音義分明，俾讀者易曉。」

translations.literal: You should consider adding circles and dots beside the characters to make sound and meaning distinct, so readers may understand easily.
translations.idiomatic: Add circles and dots beside characters to distinguish sounds and meanings for easier reading."

sentences.zh: 達海承命尋繹，字旁加圈點。

translations.literal: Dahai received the order and worked it out, adding circles and dots beside the characters.
translations.idiomatic: Dahai obeyed and devised circles and dots beside the characters.

sentences.zh: 又以國書與漢字對音，補所未備，謂：「舊有十二字頭為正字，新補為外字，猶不能盡協，則以兩字合音為一字，較漢文翻切尤精當。」

translations.literal: He also matched the national script to Chinese pronunciation to supply what was still lacking, saying: "The old twelve heads are the standard characters; the new additions are outer characters; where these still cannot fully agree, two characters may be combined in sound as one character—more precise than Chinese fanqie."
translations.idiomatic: He also aligned the script with Chinese phonology, saying: "The original twelve heads are standard forms; new supplements are outer characters; where these fail, two letters may fuse into one—finer than Chinese fanqie."

sentences.zh: 國書始大備。

translations.literal: The national script was then fully complete.
translations.idiomatic: The national script was now complete.

sentences.zh: 是年六月，達海病，踰月病亟。

translations.literal: In the sixth month of that year Dahai fell ill; after more than a month his illness became critical.
translations.idiomatic: That sixth month Dahai fell ill; after a month he was near death.

sentences.zh: 上聞，垂涕，遣侍臣往視，賜蟒緞，並諭當優恤其子。

translations.literal: When the emperor heard, he wept, sent attendants to visit him, bestowed python robes, and ordered that his son should be generously cared for.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor wept, sent visitors, granted python robes, and ordered his son well provided for.

sentences.zh: 達海聞命感愴，已不能言，數日遂卒，年三十八。

translations.literal: Hearing the decree Dahai was moved to grief; he could no longer speak and died within days, aged thirty-eight.
translations.idiomatic: Moved by the decree he could no longer speak and died within days at thirty-eight.

sentences.zh: 時方譯通鑑、六韜、孟子、三國志、大乘經，皆未竟。

translations.literal: At the time they were still translating the Comprehensive Mirror, Six Secret Teachings, Mencius, Records of the Three Kingdoms, and the Mahayana Sutra—all unfinished.
translations.idiomatic: Translation of the Comprehensive Mirror, Six Secret Teachings, Mencius, Three Kingdoms, and Mahayana Sutra remained unfinished.

sentences.zh: 無完者。

translations.literal: None was complete.
translations.idiomatic: None was finished.

sentences.zh: 七年二月，以其長子雅？

translations.literal: In the second month of the seventh year, his eldest son Yaqin
translations.idiomatic: In the second month of the seventh year his eldest son Yaqin

sentences.zh: 達海廉謹，在文館久，為領袖。

translations.literal: Dahai was upright and cautious; he had long been in the Literary Bureau and was its leader.
translations.idiomatic: Dahai was prudent and long headed the Literary Bureau.

sentences.zh: 其卒也，當斂，求秦降一等襲職，授備禦。

translations.literal: At his death, when he was to be laid in the coffin, Yaqin asked to inherit one rank lower and was appointed beiyu.
translations.idiomatic: At his burial Yaqin sought a one-rank reduction and received beiyu rank.

sentences.zh: 國初文臣無世職，有之自達海始。

translations.literal: At the founding of the dynasty civil officials had no hereditary offices; this began with Dahai.
translations.idiomatic: Civil hereditary rank began with Dahai.

sentences.zh: 十年，賜諡文成。

translations.literal: In the tenth year he was granted the posthumous name Wencheng.
translations.idiomatic: In year 10 he received the posthumous name Wencheng.

sentences.zh: 康熙八年五月，聖祖從其孫禪布請，立碑紀績。

translations.literal: In the fifth month of the eighth year of Kangxi, the Sage Emperor, at the request of his grandson Chanbu, erected a stele recording his achievements.
translations.idiomatic: In Kangxi 8, at grandson Chanbu's request, the emperor erected a memorial stele.

sentences.zh: 達海子四，長子雅秦，以備禦兼管佐領。

translations.literal: Dahai had four sons; the eldest, Yaqin, held beiyu rank and also managed an assistant captaincy.
translations.idiomatic: Dahai's eldest son Yaqin held beiyu rank and an assistant captaincy.

sentences.zh: 崇德三年，從伐明，毀董家口邊牆入，略明畿內，下山東，所向克捷。

translations.literal: In the third year of Chongde he followed the Ming campaign, broke through the border wall at Dongjiakou, raided the Ming metropolitan region, descended into Shandong, and wherever he went prevailed.
translations.idiomatic: In Chongde 3 he breached the wall at Dongjiakou, raided the capital region and Shandong, and won everywhere.

sentences.zh: 還，出青山口，遇明軍，雅秦率步兵擊敗之。

translations.literal: On the return, exiting Qingshan Pass, he met Ming troops and Yaqin led infantry and defeated them.
translations.idiomatic: Returning through Qingshan Pass he met Ming forces and routed them with infantry.

sentences.zh: 四年，從攻松山。

translations.literal: In the fourth year he followed the attack on Songshan.
translations.idiomatic: In year 4 he joined the Songshan siege.

sentences.zh: 六年，從圍錦州，城兵突出犯我軍，雅秦率所部兵禦敵，皆有功。

translations.literal: In the sixth year he followed the siege of Jinzhou; garrison troops sallied against our army and Yaqin led his troops to repel the enemy—all with merit.
translations.idiomatic: In year 6 at Jinzhou he repelled sallies with merit.

sentences.zh: 旋授吏部理事官。

translations.literal: He was soon appointed a Board of Personnel administrative officer.
translations.idiomatic: He soon became a Personnel administrative officer.

sentences.zh: 八年，調戶部理事官。

translations.literal: In the eighth year he was transferred to the Board of Revenue.
translations.idiomatic: In year 8 he moved to Revenue.

sentences.zh: 順治元年四月，從入關，擊敗李自成。

translations.literal: In the fourth month of the first year of Shunzhi he followed the entry into the pass and defeated Li Zicheng.
translations.idiomatic: In Shunzhi 1 he entered the pass and defeated Li Zicheng.

sentences.zh: 迭遇恩詔，進世職至二等阿思哈尼哈番。

translations.literal: On successive amnesty edicts his hereditary rank rose to second-rank ashanihafan.
translations.idiomatic: Amnesty edicts raised his hereditary rank to second-rank ashanihafan.

sentences.zh: 八年三月，授吏部侍郎。

translations.literal: In the third month of the eighth year he was appointed vice minister of the Board of Personnel.
translations.idiomatic: In the third month of year 8 he became Personnel vice minister.

sentences.zh: 七月，擢國史院大學士。

translations.literal: In the seventh month he was promoted to Grand Secretary of the Historiography Institute.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh month he rose to Historiography Grand Secretary.

sentences.zh: 十月，卒。

translations.literal: In the tenth month he died.
translations.idiomatic: He died in the tenth month.

sentences.zh: 九年，上以恩詔進世職過濫，命改為一等阿達哈哈番兼拖沙喇哈番。

translations.literal: In the ninth year, because amnesty promotions of hereditary rank had become excessive, the emperor ordered it changed to first-rank adahafan with toshalahafan.
translations.idiomatic: In year 9 the throne curtailed amnesty inflation, resetting his rank to first adahafan with toshalahafan.

sentences.zh: 予其子禪布襲職。

translations.literal: His son Chanbu was granted the inheritance.
translations.idiomatic: Son Chanbu inherited the office.

sentences.zh: 康熙二十一年，聖祖巡方，命從官祭雅秦墓。

translations.literal: In the twenty-first year of Kangxi, when the Sage Emperor toured the regions, he ordered accompanying officials to sacrifice at Yaqin's tomb.
translations.idiomatic: On Kangxi 21's imperial tour officials sacrificed at Yaqin's tomb.

sentences.zh: 達海次子辰德，太宗嘗召其兄弟，賜饌予幣，命辰德勤習漢文，其後仕未顯。

translations.literal: Dahai's second son Chende: Taizong once summoned the brothers, gave them food and gifts, and ordered Chende to study Chinese diligently; afterward his career was not distinguished.
translations.idiomatic: Second son Chende was urged to study Chinese by Taizong but never rose prominently.

sentences.zh: 三子喇捫，康熙間，以前鋒統領從討吳三桂，戰衡州，陣沒，贈拖沙喇哈番。

translations.literal: The third son, Lamen: in the Kangxi period, as vanguard commander on the campaign against Wu Sangui, he was killed in battle at Hengzhou and was posthumously granted toshalahafan.
translations.idiomatic: Third son Lamen died at Hengzhou fighting Wu Sangui and received posthumous toshalahafan.

sentences.zh: 四子常額，雅秦卒後，世祖特授學士，而雅秦子禪布，康熙初亦官秘書院學士，為達海請立碑。

translations.literal: The fourth son, Changer: after Yaqin's death the Shizu Emperor specially appointed him bachelor; Yaqin's son Chanbu in early Kangxi also served as bachelor of the Secretariat and petitioned for Dahai's stele.
translations.idiomatic: Fourth son Changer became bachelor after Yaqin's death; grandson Chanbu petitioned for Dahai's stele.

sentences.zh: 三桂既平之明年，聖祖諮諸大學士：「達海巴克什子孫有入仕者乎？」

translations.literal: The year after the Three Feudatories were pacified, the Sage Emperor asked the grand secretaries: "Are there descendants of Bakshi Dahai in office?"
translations.idiomatic: After the rebellion was crushed the emperor asked whether Dahai's descendants still served.

sentences.zh: 明珠對：「聞有孫為鴻臚寺官。」

translations.literal: Mingju replied: "I hear a grandson holds office in the Court of Imperial Entertainments."
translations.idiomatic: Mingju said a grandson served in the Court of Imperial Entertainments.

sentences.zh: 因下吏部錄達海諸孫陳布祿等十二人引見，命授陳布祿刑部郎中。

translations.literal: Thereupon the Board of Personnel was ordered to register Dahai's grandsons Chenbulu and eleven others for audience, and Chenbulu was appointed a director in the Board of Punishments.
translations.idiomatic: Twelve grandsons including Chenbulu were presented; Chenbulu became a Punishments director.

sentences.zh: 其後國子監祭酒阿理瑚請以達海從祀孔子廟，禮部尚書韓菼議不可，乃罷。

translations.literal: Later Grand Master of the National Academy Arihu asked that Dahai be enshrined in the Confucian temple; Minister of Rites Han Tan ruled against it and the proposal was dropped.
translations.idiomatic: A later proposal to enshrine Dahai in Confucius's temple was rejected by Rites Minister Han Tan.

sentences.zh: 達海以增定國書，滿洲？

translations.literal: Because Dahai expanded and fixed the national script, the Manchu
translations.idiomatic: For refining the national script Manchu

sentences.zh: 推為聖人。

translations.literal: honored him as a sage.
translations.idiomatic: honored him as a sage.

sentences.zh: 其子孫：男子系紫帶，亞於宗姓；

translations.literal: His descendants: men wore purple belts, ranking below the imperial clan;
translations.idiomatic: Male descendants wore purple belts below imperial clansmen;

sentences.zh: 女子不選秀女。

translations.literal: women were not selected as palace candidates.
translations.idiomatic: their women were exempt from palace selection.

sentences.zh: 尼堪，納喇氏，世居松阿里烏喇。

translations.literal: Nikan, of the Nara clan, whose family had long resided at Songali Wula.
translations.idiomatic: Nikan of the Nara clan came from Songali Wula.

sentences.zh: 太祖時來歸，賜號「巴克什」。

translations.literal: He came over in submission in the time of Taizu and was granted the title "Bakshi."
translations.idiomatic: He submitted under Taizu and received the title Bakshi.

sentences.zh: 旗制定，隸滿洲鑲博爾晉等率師伐虎爾哈部，收五？

translations.literal: When the banners were fixed he was enrolled in the Manchu Bordered Bo'erjin and others led troops against the Hurka tribe and brought back five
translations.idiomatic: When banners were fixed he joined the Bordered White Banner. He followed Bo'erjin against the Hurka and returned with five

sentences.zh: 白旗。

translations.literal: hundred-odd households.
translations.idiomatic: hundred-odd households.

sentences.zh: 初以說降蒙古科爾沁部，授備禦。

translations.literal: At first, for persuading the Mongol Khorchin tribe to submit, he was appointed beiyu.
translations.idiomatic: For talking the Khorchin Mongols into submission he received beiyu rank.

sentences.zh: 天命十年，偕侍百戶以還，上郊勞賜宴。

translations.literal: In the tenth year of Tianming he returned with a hundred household attendants; the emperor met him outside the capital and granted a banquet.
translations.idiomatic: In Tianming 10 he returned with a hundred attendants and was feasted outside the capital.
He then served on later campaigns.

sentences.zh: 從太宗伐明，攻錦州，有功。

translations.literal: He followed Taizong's campaign against Ming, attacked Jinzhou, and had merit.
translations.idiomatic: He joined Taizong's Ming campaigns and served at Jinzhou.

sentences.zh: 七年，從諸貝勒按獄蒙古諸部，？

translations.literal: In the seventh year he followed the princes in judging cases among the Mongol tribes;
translations.idiomatic: In year 7 he joined princes judging Mongol cases;

sentences.zh: 天聰初，擢一等侍牛錄額真阿什達爾漢以所齎敕二十道付尼堪，尼堪以授從者，失其九。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Tiancong he was promoted to first-rank attendant. Niru captain Ashadahan handed him twenty imperial edicts to deliver; Nikan gave them to his followers and lost nine.
translations.idiomatic: at Tiancong's opening he rose to first-rank attendant. Ashadahan gave him twenty edicts; he passed them to followers and lost nine.

sentences.zh: 所司論劾，罰如律。

translations.literal: The responsible office impeached him and he was punished according to law.
translations.idiomatic: Impeachment brought legal punishment.

sentences.zh: 蒿齊忒部台吉額林等來歸，命尼堪往迎。

translations.literal: When the Haqitai chieftain Elin and others came over in submission, Nikan was ordered to go welcome them.
translations.idiomatic: When Haqitai chief Elin submitted, Nikan was sent to welcome him.

sentences.zh: 八年正月，收其部落戶口、牲畜以還。

translations.literal: In the first month of the eighth year he returned with the tribes' households and livestock.
translations.idiomatic: In the first month of year 8 he returned with tribes and livestock.

sentences.zh: 七月，上伐來歸，命尼堪還盛京安置。

translations.literal: In the seventh month, as the emperor attacked those who had submitted, Nikan was ordered back to Shengjing to settle them.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh month, while the emperor campaigned, Nikan was sent to settle returnees at Shengjing.

sentences.zh: 時鄭親王濟爾哈朗留守，使尼堪偕卦爾察、？

translations.literal: At that time Prince Zheng Jirhala was left to guard the capital; he sent Nikan with Guarcia and
translations.idiomatic: Prince Zheng Jirhala, guarding the capital, sent Nikan with Guarcia and

sentences.zh: 明，道遇察哈爾部席特庫率兵十二人偵明兵。

translations.literal: Sun Daire to attack Ming; on the road they met Xiteku of the Chahar with twelve men scouting for Ming troops.
translations.idiomatic: Sun Daire against Ming; en route they met Chahar Xiteku scouting with twelve men.

sentences.zh: 明兵適至，奮擊敗之，逐至遼河，凡三戰，斬馘百餘，明兵引退。

translations.literal: Ming troops happened to arrive; they fought fiercely and defeated them, pursued to the Liao River, fought three battles, killed and captured more than a hundred, and the Ming army withdrew.
translations.idiomatic: Ming troops appeared; they fought thrice to the Liao, killed over a hundred, and drove Ming off.

sentences.zh: 九年，從貝勒岳託戍歸化城，土默特部私與明通，岳託使尼堪及參領阿爾津伺塞上，得明使四輩、土默特使十輩，皆執以歸。

translations.literal: In the ninth year he followed Prince Yueto to garrison Guihua City; the Tumed tribe secretly communicated with Ming; Yueto sent Nikan and Commissioner Arjin to watch the frontier, seized four Ming envoys and ten Tumed envoys, and brought them back.
translations.idiomatic: In year 9 at Guihua he helped Yueto seize four Ming and ten Tumed envoys colluding on the border.

sentences.zh: 尋與英俄爾岱等使朝鮮。

translations.literal: Soon he went on embassy to Korea with Ying'e'erdai and others.
translations.idiomatic: He soon joined Ying'e'erdai on embassy to Korea.

sentences.zh: 崇德元年六月，授理籓院承政。

translations.literal: In the sixth month of the first year of Chongde he was appointed chief of the Court of Colonial Affairs.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth month of Chongde 1 he became Colonial Affairs chief.

sentences.zh: 二年正月，太宗伐朝鮮，既克其都，命尼堪及吉思哈、葉克舒帥師？

translations.literal: In the first month of the second year Taizong attacked Korea; after taking the capital he ordered Nikan with Jisiha and Yekešu to command troops
translations.idiomatic: In the second year's first month, after Korea's capital fell, Nikan, Jisiha, and Yekešu were ordered to lead

sentences.zh: 護科爾沁、扎魯特、敖漢、柰曼諸部兵伐瓦爾喀，將出朝鮮境，朝鮮兵屯吉木海，阻師行，尼堪督兵進擊，大破之，斬平壤巡撫。

translations.literal: to escort Khorchin, Jarud, Aohan, and Naiman troops against the Warka; as they were about to leave Korea, Korean troops held Jihaihai and blocked the march; Nikan directed the advance, routed them completely, and beheaded the Pyongyang governor.
translations.idiomatic: Khorchin, Jarud, Aohan, and Naiman auxiliaries against Warka; blocked at Jihaihai, he broke Korean lines and killed Pyongyang's governor.

sentences.zh: 既，朝鮮兵二萬餘人復來追襲，尼堪等設伏誘敵，殲萬餘人。

translations.literal: Afterward more than twenty thousand Korean troops came in pursuit; Nikan and others set an ambush, lured the enemy, and destroyed more than ten thousand.
translations.idiomatic: When twenty thousand Koreans pursued, he ambushed and destroyed over ten thousand.

sentences.zh: 敵遁，據山巔立柵拒守，師圍之三日，遂下。

translations.literal: The enemy fled, held the mountain crest with palisades, and resisted; the army besieged three days and then took it.
translations.idiomatic: Fleeing enemies held a hilltop fort; after three days' siege it fell.

sentences.zh: 降哈忙城巡撫及總兵副使以下官，獲牲畜、布帛諸物無算。

translations.literal: They surrendered the Hamang city governor and officials down to vice commander; livestock, cloth, and goods captured were beyond count.
translations.idiomatic: They took Hamang's governor and officers and incalculable booty.

sentences.zh: 進略瓦爾喀部，以所獲畀蒙古諸部兵，尋引師還。

translations.literal: They advanced against the Warka tribe, gave the spoils to the Mongol allied troops, and soon led the army back.
translations.idiomatic: Advancing into Warka they distributed spoils to Mongols and withdrew.

sentences.zh: 复偕阿什達爾漢使科爾沁、巴林、扎魯特、喀喇沁諸部頒赦詔，會諸部王貝勒清庶獄。

translations.literal: He again went with Ashadahan to Khorchin, Barin, Jarud, and Khalkha to proclaim amnesty edicts and convene princes and beiles to clear prisons.
translations.idiomatic: With Ashadahan he proclaimed amnesty across Khorchin, Barin, Jarud, and Khalkha and cleared prisons.

sentences.zh: 三年五月，坐讞獄科爾沁失實，解任。

translations.literal: In the fifth month of the third year, for judging a Khorchin case untruthfully, he was removed from office.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth month of year 3 false judgment in a Khorchin case cost him his post.

sentences.zh: 七月，授理籓院右參政。

translations.literal: In the seventh month he was appointed right vice commissioner of the Court of Colonial Affairs.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh month he became right vice commissioner of Colonial Affairs.

sentences.zh: 四年，伐明，徵蒙古諸部兵，兵至不如額，命尼堪使科爾沁、喀喇沁、土默特諸部詰責。

translations.literal: In the fourth year, on the Ming campaign, Mongol allied troops fell short of quota; Nikan was sent to Khorchin, Khalkha, and Tumed to reprimand them.
translations.idiomatic: In year 4, when Mongol levies fell short, he was sent to rebuke Khorchin, Khalkha, and Tumed.

sentences.zh: 五年四月，上以尼堪充副任使，授三等，編為八牛錄。

translations.literal: In the fifth month the emperor, deeming Nikan fit for deputy envoy duty, granted third rank and organized eight niru for him.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth month of year 5 he received third rank and eight niru as deputy envoy.

sentences.zh: 七月，復命徵蒙古諸部？

translations.literal: In the seventh month he was again ordered to levy Mongol allied troops and was made
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh month he was again ordered to levy Mongols and was made

sentences.zh: 甲喇章京。

translations.literal: jalan commander.
translations.idiomatic: jalan commander.

sentences.zh: 復命安集索倫、郭爾羅斯兩部新附之兵伐索倫，簡其軍實。

translations.literal: He was again ordered to settle the newly submitted Solon and Gorlos troops and campaign against the Solon, reviewing their military strength.
translations.idiomatic: He also settled newly submitted Solon and Gorlos troops and campaigned against Solon, inspecting their forces.

sentences.zh: 世祖定鼎，論功，進二等。

translations.literal: When the Shizu Emperor fixed the capital, merit was assessed and he was promoted to second rank.
translations.idiomatic: At the dynasty's founding his merit earned second rank.

sentences.zh: 順治二年，從豫親王多鐸下河南，將蒙古兵自南陽趨歸德。

translations.literal: In the second year of Shunzhi he followed Prince Yoto south into Henan and led Mongol troops from Nanyang toward Guide.
translations.idiomatic: In Shunzhi 2 he followed Yoto into Henan and led Mongols from Nanyang toward Guide.

sentences.zh: 四年，論功，進三？

translations.literal: In the fourth year, for merit, he was promoted to third
translations.idiomatic: In year 4 merit raised him to third rank;

sentences.zh: ，降州一、縣四。

translations.literal: rank; one prefecture and four counties surrendered.
translations.idiomatic: one prefecture and four counties submitted.

sentences.zh: 論功，進一等。

translations.literal: For merit he was promoted to first rank.
translations.idiomatic: For further merit he reached first rank.

sentences.zh: 三年，從多鐸討蘇尼特部，大破其等阿思哈尼哈番。

translations.literal: In the third year he followed Duo Duo against the Sunite tribe and routed them completely, etc., ashanihafan.
translations.idiomatic: In year 3 he followed Duo Duo against the Sunite and crushed them, reaching ashanihafan.

sentences.zh: 遷理籓院尚書。

translations.literal: He was transferred to minister of the Court of Colonial Affairs.
translations.idiomatic: He became Colonial Affairs minister.

sentences.zh: 六年，喀爾喀使至，餽睿親王多爾袞馬，巽親王滿達海以為言，尼堪啟王，王曰：「如例云何？」

translations.literal: In the sixth year Khalkha envoys arrived and presented horses to Prince Regent Dorgon; Prince Xun Mandahai reported this; Nikan informed the prince; the prince said: "What is the precedent?"
translations.idiomatic: In year 6 Khalkha envoys gifted horses to Dorgon; Mandahai protested; Nikan cited precedent when the prince asked.

sentences.zh: 尼堪曰：「外籓職貢，例不當餽諸王。」

translations.literal: Nikan said: "Tribute from outer vassals should not be given to princes."
translations.idiomatic: Nikan replied: "Outer tribute must not go to princes."

sentences.zh: 王惡其語侵己，令內大臣議罪，奪其俸。

translations.literal: The prince resented his words as encroaching on himself, had inner ministers judge his offense, and confiscated his salary.
translations.idiomatic: The prince, offended, had ministers punish him and seized his salary.

sentences.zh: 三遇恩詔，進三等精奇尼哈番，世襲。

translations.literal: On three amnesty edicts he was promoted to third-rank jingginiha fan, inheritable.
translations.idiomatic: Three amnesties raised him to inheritable third-rank jingginiha fan.

sentences.zh: 十年，上以尼堪老，進二等，致仕。

translations.literal: In the tenth year, as Nikan was old, he was promoted to second rank and retired.
translations.idiomatic: In year 10, aged, he rose to second rank and retired.

sentences.zh: 十七年，卒。

translations.literal: In the seventeenth year he died.
translations.idiomatic: He died in year 17.

sentences.zh: 無子，以其弟阿穆爾圖、阿錫圖，從子瑪拉、兆資分襲世職。

translations.literal: Having no son, his younger brothers Amurtu and Axitu and his nephews Mara and Zhaozi divided the hereditary office.
translations.idiomatic: Childless, brothers Amurtu and Axitu and nephews Mara and Zhaozi split the inheritance.

sentences.zh: 瑪拉自有傳。

translations.literal: Mara has his own biography.
translations.idiomatic: Mara has a separate biography.

sentences.zh: 庫爾纏，鈕祜祿氏，世居長白山。

translations.literal: Ku'erchan, of the Niohuru clan, whose family had long resided at Changbai Mountain.
translations.idiomatic: Ku'erchan of the Niohuru clan came from Changbai Mountain.

sentences.zh: 祖曰賴盧渾，父曰索塔蘭。

translations.literal: His grandfather was called Nailuhun; his father was called Suotanlan.
translations.idiomatic: Grandfather Nailuhun; father Suotanlan.

sentences.zh: 賴盧渾先為哈達都督，索塔蘭及所部來歸。

translations.literal: Nailuhun had first been governor of Hada; Suotanlan and his following came over in submission.
translations.idiomatic: Nailuhun had governed Hada; Suotanlan submitted with his people.

sentences.zh: 旗制定，隸屬滿洲鑲紅旗。

translations.literal: When the banners were fixed he was enrolled in the Manchu Bordered Red Banner.
translations.idiomatic: He was assigned to the Manchu Bordered Red Banner.

sentences.zh: 太祖以女妻索塔蘭，生子四，庫爾？

translations.literal: Taizu gave his daughter in marriage to Suotanlan, who had four sons; Ku'er
translations.idiomatic: Taizu married a daughter to Suotanlan, who had four sons; Ku'erchan

sentences.zh: 其次子也。

translations.literal: chan was the second son.
translations.idiomatic: was the second.

sentences.zh: 天命元年，召直左右。

translations.literal: In the first year of Tianming he was summoned to attend at the emperor's side.
translations.idiomatic: In Tianming 1 he entered imperial attendance.

sentences.zh: 十一月，蒙古喀爾喀五部來議和，庫爾？

translations.literal: In the eleventh month the five Khalkha Mongol tribes came to negotiate peace; Ku'er
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh month five Khalkha tribes came to parley; Ku'erchan

sentences.zh: 齎書蒞盟；

translations.literal: chan carried the letter to preside over the alliance;
translations.idiomatic: carried the treaty to the parley;

sentences.zh: 九年二月，復將命如科爾沁修好：皆稱旨，授牛錄章京。

translations.literal: In the second month of the ninth year he was again sent on mission to Khorchin to restore good relations—all accorded with the imperial will, and he was appointed niru commander.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth year's second month he again treated with Khorchin to the emperor's satisfaction and received niru commander rank.

sentences.zh: 太宗即位，伐扎魯特部，庫爾？

translations.literal: When Taizong acceded he attacked the Jarud tribe; Ku'er
translations.idiomatic: When Taizong attacked Jarud, Ku'erchan

sentences.zh: 從，師還，上勞諸貝勒。

translations.literal: chan followed; when the army returned the emperor rewarded the princes.
translations.idiomatic: followed; on return the emperor feasted the princes.

sentences.zh: 飲至，達海承旨問諸貝勒行軍勝敵始末，庫爾？

translations.literal: At the drinking ceremony Dahai, by imperial order, asked the princes for the full account of the march and victories; Ku'er
translations.idiomatic: At the feast Dahai questioned princes on the campaign; Ku'erchan

sentences.zh: 為諸貝勒具對，成禮。

translations.literal: chan answered on behalf of the princes and the rite was completed.
translations.idiomatic: answered for them and the rite concluded.

sentences.zh: 天聰元年，伐朝鮮，庫爾？

translations.literal: In the first year of Tiancong he attacked Korea; Ku'er
translations.idiomatic: In Tiancong 1 on the Korea campaign Ku'erchan

sentences.zh: 從，朝鮮王李倧請行成，庫爾？

translations.literal: chan followed; King Li Jong asked to sue for peace; Ku'er
translations.idiomatic: followed; King Li Jong sued for peace; Ku'erchan

sentences.zh: 及副將劉興祚將命宣撫。

translations.literal: chan and Vice Commander Liu Xingzuo were sent to proclaim and pacify.
translations.idiomatic: and Liu Xingzuo were sent to proclaim terms.

sentences.zh: 倧既約降，庫爾？

translations.literal: After Jong had agreed to surrender, Ku'er
translations.idiomatic: After Jong agreed, Ku'erchan

sentences.zh: 等還報，朝鮮諸將不知倧已約降也，以步騎兵千人邀諸平壤，庫爾？

translations.literal: chan and others returned to report; the Korean generals did not know Jong had already agreed to surrender and with a thousand infantry and cavalry intercepted them at Pyongyang; Ku'er
translations.idiomatic: reported back; unaware Korean generals with a thousand men intercepted them at Pyongyang; Ku'erchan

sentences.zh: 集從者環甲突圍出。

translations.literal: chan gathered his followers, armored in a ring, and broke out.
translations.idiomatic: armored his escort and broke out.

sentences.zh: 朝鮮兵躡其後，庫爾？

translations.literal: Korean troops followed behind; Ku'er
translations.idiomatic: Koreans pursued; Ku'erchan

sentences.zh: 令從者前行，而以十騎殿，殺朝鮮兵三，疾馳六十里。

translations.literal: chan ordered the followers to go ahead while he with ten horsemen brought up the rear, killed three Korean soldiers, and galloped sixty li.
translations.idiomatic: sent the party ahead while ten horsemen held the rear, killed three, and rode sixty li.

sentences.zh: 朝鮮兵三百騎繼至，庫爾？

translations.literal: Three hundred Korean horsemen came up again; Ku'er
translations.idiomatic: Three hundred Korean horsemen caught up; Ku'erchan

sentences.zh: 率十騎憑？

translations.literal: chan with ten horsemen took position at a
translations.idiomatic: with ten riders held a

sentences.zh: 隘為伏，擊敗之，斬朝鮮將四、兵五十餘，獲馬百，卒達瀋陽。

translations.literal: pass and lay in ambush, defeated them, beheaded four Korean generals and more than fifty soldiers, captured a hundred horses, and finally reached Shenyang.
translations.idiomatic: defile in ambush, killed four Korean officers and fifty men, took a hundred horses, and reached Shenyang.

sentences.zh: 上復命齎諭至軍中申軍令，定盟誓而還。

translations.literal: The emperor again ordered him to carry an edict to the army to enforce military discipline, fix the alliance oath, and return.
translations.idiomatic: He was again sent to the army with edicts fixing the oath and discipline.

sentences.zh: 三年四月，定文館職守，命記註時政，備國史。

translations.literal: In the fourth month of the third year the duties of the Literary Bureau were fixed; he was ordered to record current affairs for the national history.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year's fourth month the Literary Bureau was ordered to record affairs for the national history.

sentences.zh: 四年正月，伐明，庫爾纏偕游擊高鴻中先至灤州，設謀使啟城門，師遂入。

translations.literal: In the first month of the fourth year, on the Ming campaign, Ku'erchan with Guerrilla Commander Gao Hongzhong reached Luanzhou first, used stratagem to open the gate, and the army entered.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year's first month Ku'erchan and Gao Hongzhong opened Luanzhou by stratagem and the army entered.

sentences.zh: 二月，師還，庫爾？

translations.literal: In the second month the army returned; Ku'er
translations.idiomatic: When the army withdrew in the second month Ku'erchan

sentences.zh: 從諸將戍焉。

translations.literal: chan followed the generals to garrison there.
translations.idiomatic: stayed to garrison with other commanders.

sentences.zh: 五月，明監軍道張春等來攻，庫爾？

translations.literal: In the fifth month Ming Military Circuit Commissioner Zhang Chun and others came to attack; Ku'er
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth month Zhang Chun attacked; Ku'erchan

sentences.zh: 與牛錄額真覺善等勒兵出戰，奮逾塹，直趣敵陣。

translations.literal: chan with niru captain Jueshan and others led troops out to fight, leaped the moat, and charged straight at the enemy line.
translations.idiomatic: with Jueshan sallied, crossed the moat, and charged the enemy.

sentences.zh: 春等稍卻，旋發火器焚城樓，壞睥睨，庫爾？

translations.literal: Chun and others fell back slightly, then fired weapons and burned the tower, destroying the parapet; Ku'er
translations.idiomatic: Chun briefly withdrew, then fired on the tower; Ku'erchan

sentences.zh: 與覺善還兵御之，敵不能登。

translations.literal: chan with Jueshan turned back to repel them and the enemy could not mount the wall.
translations.idiomatic: and Jueshan repulsed the assault on the walls.

sentences.zh: 都統圖爾格等以孤軍無援，退保永平，敵圍益急，庫爾？

translations.literal: Commander Turgut and others, isolated without relief, withdrew to Yongping; the siege grew tighter; Ku'er
translations.idiomatic: Isolated at Yongping as Turgut withdrew, Ku'erchan

sentences.zh: 且守且戰，屢有斬馘。

translations.literal: chan both defended and fought, repeatedly killing and capturing.
translations.idiomatic: defended and fought with repeated kills.

sentences.zh: 旋從貝勒阿敏等棄諸城，還都待罪。

translations.literal: Soon he followed Prince Amin and others in abandoning the cities, returned to the capital, and awaited punishment.
translations.idiomatic: He followed Amin in abandoning the cities and returned to await punishment.

sentences.zh: 上以在灤州時能力戰，特貰之。

translations.literal: Because at Luanzhou he had been able to fight hard, the emperor specially pardoned him.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor pardoned him for fierce fighting at Luanzhou.

sentences.zh: 庫爾纏先以口語被訐。

translations.literal: Ku'erchan had earlier been impeached for colloquial speech.
translations.idiomatic: Ku'erchan had earlier been denounced for loose speech.

sentences.zh: 五年十一月，使朝鮮，以漢文作書遺朝鮮，受私餽。

translations.literal: In the eleventh month of the fifth year he was sent to Korea, wrote a letter in Chinese to Korea, and accepted private gifts.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth year's eleventh month he went to Korea, wrote in Chinese, and took private gifts.

sentences.zh: 六年六月，使明得勝堡議和，以其人來，上召入見，屢失期。

translations.literal: In the sixth month of the sixth year he was sent to Desheng Fort in Ming to negotiate peace; when those people came, the emperor summoned them to audience but they repeatedly missed appointments.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth year's sixth month he treated at Ming Desheng Fort; the envoys repeatedly missed audiences.

sentences.zh: 七年二月，上發庫爾？

translations.literal: In the second month of the seventh year the emperor published Ku'er
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh year's second month the emperor published Ku'erchan's

sentences.zh: 諸罪，並追議庇劉興祚罪，論死。

translations.literal: chan's crimes and also pursued the charge of shielding Liu Xingzuo; he was sentenced to death.
translations.idiomatic: crimes, added shielding Liu Xingzuo, and sentenced him to death.

sentences.zh: 興祚者開原人，見辱開原道，遂率其諸弟興治等以降，太祖以國語名之曰愛塔。

translations.literal: Xingzuo was a native of Kaiyuan; humiliated by the Kaiyuan circuit intendant, he led his brothers Xingzhi and others to surrender; Taizu named him in the national language Aita.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Xingzuo of Kaiyuan, humiliated by local officials, surrendered with his brothers; Taizu called him Aita.

sentences.zh: 克遼東，授副將，領蓋、复、金三州。

translations.literal: When Liaodong was taken he was made vice commander and governed Gaizhou, Fuzhou, and Jinzhou.
translations.idiomatic: After Liaodong fell he governed three prefectures as vice commander.

sentences.zh: 興祚婪，索民財畜，被訐解任，遂有叛志。

translations.literal: Xingzuo was greedy, extorted people's goods and livestock, was impeached and removed, and then harbored rebellious intent.
translations.idiomatic: Greedy and extortionate, he was removed and turned rebel.

sentences.zh: 事屢敗，太宗屢覆蓋之。

translations.literal: Matters repeatedly failed; Taizong repeatedly covered for him.
translations.idiomatic: Repeated plots failed yet Taizong shielded him.

sentences.zh: 興祚使其弟興賢逃歸毛文龍，作書遺庫爾？

translations.literal: Xingzuo had his brother Xingxian flee back to Mao Wenlong and wrote a letter to Ku'er
translations.idiomatic: Xingzuo sent Xingxian to Mao Wenlong and wrote Ku'erchan

sentences.zh: ，詭言且死，託以營葬，誑瞽者醉而縊殺之，焚其室逸去。

translations.literal: , falsely saying he was about to die and entrusting burial; he deceived a blind man, got him drunk, strangled and killed him, burned the house, and escaped.
translations.idiomatic: claiming imminent death; he strangled a blind man, burned the house, and fled.

sentences.zh: 庫爾？

translations.literal: Ku'er
translations.idiomatic: Ku'erchan

sentences.zh: 得書，視興祚，見瞽者屍，以為興祚也，持之慟，告於上，以其子五十襲職，為營葬。

translations.literal: chan received the letter, looked at Xingzuo, saw the blind man's corpse, thought it was Xingzuo, mourned bitterly, reported to the emperor, had Xingzuo's son Wushi inherit the office, and arranged burial.
translations.idiomatic: received the letter, saw the corpse, mourned as for Xingzuo, had his son inherit, and arranged burial.

sentences.zh: 既而其弟興治亦遁，詐漸露。

translations.literal: Afterward his brother Xingzhi also fled and the fraud gradually came to light.
translations.idiomatic: When Xingzhi also fled the fraud emerged.

sentences.zh: 興祚、興治去事文龍，文龍薦為參將。

translations.literal: Xingzuo and Xingzhi went to serve Wenlong; Wenlong recommended them as commanders.
translations.idiomatic: Both brothers served Wenlong as recommended commanders.

sentences.zh: 袁崇煥殺文龍，使興治及陳繼盛分將其兵。

translations.literal: Yuan Chonghuan killed Wenlong and had Xingzhi and Chen Jisheng divide his troops.
translations.idiomatic: Yuan Chonghuan killed Wenlong and split his forces between Xingzhi and Chen Jisheng.

sentences.zh: 天聰四年，上攻永平，興祚在敵中，襲我軍中喀喇沁兵，殺數十人。

translations.literal: In the fourth year of Tiancong, when the attack mounted on Yongping, Xingzuo was among the enemy and raided our Kharchin troops in camp, killing several tens.
translations.idiomatic: In Tiancong 4 at Yongping Xingzuo raided Kharchin troops and killed dozens.

sentences.zh: 使貝勒阿巴泰、濟爾哈朗將五百人求興祚。

translations.literal: Princes Abatai and Jirhala were sent with five hundred men to seek Xingzuo.
translations.idiomatic: Abatai and Jirhala were sent with five hundred men after him.

sentences.zh: 興祚將趨山海關，阿巴泰遮其前，濟爾哈朗迫其後，遂戰，甲喇額真圖魯什獲興祚，殺之，執興賢以歸。

translations.literal: Xingzuo was about to flee toward Shanhaiguan; Abatai blocked his front and Jirhala pressed his rear; they fought; jalan commander Tulushi captured Xingzuo, killed him, and brought Xingxian back.
translations.idiomatic: Abatai and Jirhala trapped him; Tulushi captured and killed Xingzuo and took Xingxian.

sentences.zh: 庫爾？

translations.literal: Ku'er
translations.idiomatic: Ku'erchan

sentences.zh: 解衣瘞興祚，上命發而磔之，庫爾？

translations.literal: chan removed his robe to bury Xingzuo; the emperor ordered the body exhumed and dismembered; Ku'er
translations.idiomatic: stripped his robe to bury Xingzuo; the emperor ordered dismemberment; Ku'erchan

sentences.zh: 复竊收其遺骼。

translations.literal: chan again secretly gathered the scattered bones.
translations.idiomatic: again secretly gathered the bones.

sentences.zh: 時興治將兵駐皮島，諸弟興基、興梁、興沛、興邦皆為偏裨。

translations.literal: At that time Xingzhi commanded troops stationed on Pidao; brothers Xingji, Xingliang, Xingpei, and Xingbang were all junior officers.
translations.idiomatic: Xingzhi held Pidao while brothers served as officers.

sentences.zh: 興沛以游擊守長山島，上遣使招興治等，諱言邏卒誤殺興祚；

translations.literal: Xingpei as guerrilla commander guarded Changshan Island; the emperor sent envoys to summon Xingzhi and others, concealing that border troops had mistakenly killed Xingzuo;
translations.idiomatic: Envoys summoned Xingzhi, claiming border troops had mistakenly killed Xingzuo;

sentences.zh: 且令興賢附書述上恩，贍其母及妻。

translations.literal: and had Xingxian attach a letter describing the emperor's grace and providing for his mother and wife.
translations.idiomatic: Xingxian's letter promised grace for mother and wife.

sentences.zh: 使屢返，復遣護其妻以往，興治亦屢答上書，自署「客國臣」，枝梧不得要領。

translations.literal: Envoys returned repeatedly; again the wife was escorted there; Xingzhi also repeatedly answered with letters, signing himself "subject of a guest state," evading the main point.
translations.idiomatic: Xingzhi answered evasively as "subject of a guest state."

sentences.zh: 會興治為興祚發喪，而繼盛信諜言，疑未死，興治忿，執殺繼盛，因縱掠。

translations.literal: When Xingzhi held mourning for Xingzuo and Jisheng believed spy reports that he was not dead, Xingzhi in anger seized and killed Jisheng and then plundered freely.
translations.idiomatic: At Xingzuo's funeral Jisheng doubted he was dead; Xingzhi killed Jisheng and plundered.

sentences.zh: 明使黃龍鎮皮島，興治復為亂，被殺。

translations.literal: Ming sent Huang Long to garrison Pidao; Xingzhi again rebelled and was killed.
translations.idiomatic: Huang Long garrisoned Pidao; Xingzhi rebelled again and was killed.

sentences.zh: 上亦殺興賢及其諸子。

translations.literal: The emperor also killed Xingxian and his sons.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor executed Xingxian and his sons.

sentences.zh: 庫爾？

translations.literal: Ku'er
translations.idiomatic: Ku'erchan

sentences.zh: 與興祚善，未叛，屢為上言，終收其骨，卒以此及。

translations.literal: chan was on good terms with Xingzuo; though he had not rebelled, he repeatedly spoke for him to the emperor and finally recovered his bones—yet in the end he was implicated for this.
translations.idiomatic: befriended Xingzuo, never rebelled, yet pleaded for him, recovered his bones, and was condemned.

sentences.zh: 上猶念其有勞，命毋籍其家。

translations.literal: The emperor still remembered his service and ordered that his household not be confiscated.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor spared his household from confiscation.

sentences.zh: 世祖定鼎燕京，詔視一品大臣例，予宅地、奴僕。

translations.literal: When the Shizu Emperor fixed the capital at Yanjing, an edict granted him residence and slaves by the precedent for a first-rank minister.
translations.idiomatic: At Yanjing he received a grand minister's residence and slaves.

sentences.zh: 庫爾？

translations.literal: Ku'er
translations.idiomatic: Ku'erchan's

sentences.zh: 弟庫拜，初以小校事太祖，從伐明，取撫順，戰敗追兵，復下遼、瀋，命為牛錄額真。

translations.literal: chan's younger brother Kubai at first served Taizu as a petty officer; he followed the Ming campaign, took Fushun, fought off pursuing troops, and again took Liaoyang and Shenyang; he was appointed niru captain.
translations.idiomatic: younger brother Kubai, a petty officer under Taizu, fought at Fushun and Liaodong and became niru captain.

sentences.zh: 天聰五年，從伐瓦爾喀，手被創，猶力戰，克堡一。

translations.literal: In the fifth year of Tiancong he followed the Warka campaign; though wounded in the hand he still fought hard and took one fort.
translations.idiomatic: In Tiancong 5 on the Warka campaign he fought wounded and took a fort.

sentences.zh: 是年七月，初設六部，授吏部參政。

translations.literal: In the seventh month of that year the Six Boards were first established and he was appointed vice commissioner of the Board of Personnel.
translations.idiomatic: That seventh month he became Personnel vice commissioner when the Six Boards opened.

translations.literal: For
translations.idiomatic: For

sentences.zh: 功，授牛錄章京世職。

translations.literal: merit he was granted the hereditary office of niru commander.
translations.idiomatic: merit he received hereditary niru commander rank.

sentences.zh: 復以吏部考滿，授三等甲喇章京。

translations.literal: Again, on completing his term at the Board of Personnel, he was made third-rank jalan commander.
translations.idiomatic: Personnel term completion brought third-rank jalan rank.

sentences.zh: 八年，從伐黑龍江諸部。

translations.literal: In the eighth year he followed the campaign against the Heilongjiang tribes.
translations.idiomatic: In year 8 he campaigned on the Heilongjiang.

sentences.zh: 九年，進二等甲喇章京。

translations.literal: In the ninth year he was promoted to second-rank jalan commander.
translations.idiomatic: In year 9 he rose to second-rank jalan.

sentences.zh: 崇德元年，從伐朝鮮。

translations.literal: In the first year of Chongde he followed the Korea campaign.
translations.idiomatic: In Chongde 1 he joined the Korea campaign.

sentences.zh: 追論伐瓦爾喀時奪部卒俘，復令部卒私獵，論罰，罷牛錄章京。

translations.literal: Retrospectively judged for seizing subordinates' captives on the Warka campaign and letting subordinates hunt privately, he was punished and removed from niru commander.
translations.idiomatic: Retrospective charges over Warka captives and private hunting cost him his niru command.

sentences.zh: 三年七月，更定官制，改吏部理事官。

translations.literal: In the seventh month of the third year the official system was revised and he was made Board of Personnel administrative officer.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year's seventh month he became Personnel administrative officer.

sentences.zh: 五年正月，卒。

translations.literal: In the first month of the fifth year he died.
translations.idiomatic: He died in the fifth year's first month.

sentences.zh: 英俄爾岱，他塔喇氏，世居扎庫木。

translations.literal: Ying'e'erdai, of the Tatara clan, whose family had long resided at Zhakumu.
translations.idiomatic: Ying'e'erdai of the Tatara clan came from Zhakumu.

sentences.zh: 太祖時，從其祖岱圖庫哈理來歸，授牛錄額真，隸滿洲正白旗。

translations.literal: In the time of Taizu he followed his grandfather Daitukuhali in coming over in submission, was appointed niru captain, and was enrolled in the Manchu Plain White Banner.
translations.idiomatic: Under Taizu he followed grandfather Daitukuhali, submitted, and joined the Plain White Banner.

sentences.zh: 天命四年，從攻開原。

translations.literal: In the fourth year of Tianming he followed the attack on Kaiyuan.
translations.idiomatic: In Tianming 4 he joined the Kaiyuan attack.

sentences.zh: 有蒙古巴圖魯阿布爾者，素以驍勇名，降明為邊將，出戰，英俄爾岱馳斬之。

translations.literal: There was a Mongol baturu named Abur, famed for valor; he surrendered to Ming and became a frontier general; going out to fight, Ying'e'erdai galloped up and beheaded him.
translations.idiomatic: He killed the famed Mongol warrior Abur, who had defected to Ming.

sentences.zh: 六年，從克瀋陽，授游擊。

translations.literal: In the sixth year he followed the capture of Shenyang and was appointed guerrilla commander.
translations.idiomatic: In year 6 at Shenyang he received guerrilla rank.

sentences.zh: 從克遼陽，授二等參將。

translations.literal: Following the capture of Liaoyang he was appointed second-rank vice commander.
translations.idiomatic: After Liaoyang he became second-rank vice commander.

sentences.zh: 天聰三年，從伐明，克遵化，太宗督諸軍向明都，而令英俄爾岱及李思忠、範文程以兵八百守遵化。

translations.literal: In the third year of Tiancong he followed the Ming campaign, took Zunhua; Taizong led the main army toward the Ming capital while Ying'e'erdai with Li Sizhong and Fan Wencheng held Zunhua with eight hundred men.
translations.idiomatic: In Tiancong 3 he took Zunhua while Taizong marched on Beijing; Ying'e'erdai, Li Sizhong, and Fan Wencheng held it with eight hundred men.

sentences.zh: 師既行，所下諸城堡石門驛、馬蘭峪、三屯營，大安口、羅文峪、漢兒莊、郭家峪、洪山口、潘家口、灤陽營皆復為明守。

translations.literal: After the army marched, the captured forts Shimen Post, Malanyu, Santunying, Daankou, Luowenyu, Han'erzhuang, Guojiayu, Hongshankou, Panjiakou, and Luanyangying all reverted to Ming garrisons.
translations.idiomatic: After the main army left, many captured forts reverted to Ming.

sentences.zh: 明兵夜薄遵化，英俄爾岱率兵擊卻之。

translations.literal: Ming troops pressed Zunhua by night; Ying'e'erdai led troops and drove them back.
translations.idiomatic: Ming pressed Zunhua by night; he drove them back.

sentences.zh: 平旦悉銳奮擊，明兵退，斬殿？

translations.literal: At dawn he mustered his best troops and attacked fiercely; the Ming army withdrew; he beheaded the rear-guard
translations.idiomatic: At dawn he attacked; Ming withdrew; he killed the rear-guard

sentences.zh: ，明將以騎兵列陣待，英俄爾岱出戰，明兵驟至，英俄爾岱麾其者五人，俘材官一，明兵宵奔。

translations.literal: , and Ming generals waited in cavalry formation; Ying'e'erdai went out to fight; Ming troops suddenly arrived; Ying'e'erdai directed five of his men, captured one engineer officer, and the Ming army fled by night.
translations.idiomatic: commander; when Ming cavalry formed he fought, captured an engineer, and Ming fled by night.

sentences.zh: 英俄爾岱以師從之，复殲騎卒百、步卒千餘，以書諭諸城，羅文峪、三屯營、洪山口、漢兒莊、灤陽營五城复降。

translations.literal: Ying'e'erdai followed with the army and again destroyed a hundred cavalry and more than a thousand infantry; he sent letters to the cities and Luowenyu, Santunying, Hongshankou, Han'erzhuang, and Luanyangying five cities submitted again.
translations.idiomatic: Pursuing, he destroyed hundreds more and five cities resubmitted.

sentences.zh: 五年七月，定官制，始設六部，以英俄爾岱為戶部承政。

translations.literal: In the seventh month of the fifth year the official system was fixed, the Six Boards were first established, and Ying'e'erdai was made chief of the Board of Revenue.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth year's seventh month he became Revenue chief when the Six Boards opened.

sentences.zh: 七年，明故毛文龍部將孔有德、耿仲明自登州來降，使英俄爾岱及游擊羅奇齎書徵糧於朝鮮，朝鮮國王李倧使其臣樸祿報聘，言毛氏舊為敵，不原輸糧。

translations.literal: In the seventh year Kong Youde and Geng Zhongming, former generals of Mao Wenlong, surrendered from Dengzhou; Ying'e'erdai and Guerrilla Commander Luo Qi were sent with letters to requisition grain from Korea; King Li Jong sent his minister Piao Lu on a return embassy, saying the Mao clan had been enemies and they were unwilling to supply grain.
translations.idiomatic: In year 7 he requisitioned Korean grain for Kong Youde and Geng Zhongming; Korea refused citing old enmity with Mao.

sentences.zh: 太宗復以書諭，略言：「毛氏將今歸我國，以兵守其舟，當就便輸以糧。」

translations.literal: Taizong again wrote instructing, in summary: "The Mao generals now return to our state; troops guard their ships and grain should be supplied conveniently."
translations.idiomatic: Taizong wrote that Mao's men now served the throne and Korea should supply grain.

sentences.zh: 遣英俄爾岱及備禦代松阿齎書復往，朝鮮乃輸糧如指。

translations.literal: Ying'e'erdai and Beiyu Dai Song'a were sent with the letter again; Korea then supplied grain as directed.
translations.idiomatic: Sent again with Dai Song'a, he secured the grain.

sentences.zh: 八年五月，改進一等甲喇章京。

translations.literal: In the fifth month of the eighth year he was promoted to first-rank jalan commander.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth year's fifth month he rose to first-rank jalan.

sentences.zh: 太宗自將伐察哈爾，察哈爾林丹汗走圖白特，所部潰散。

translations.literal: Taizong personally led a campaign against the Chahar; Chahar Lind Khan fled to Tubait and his following dispersed.
translations.idiomatic: Taizong campaigned against Chahar; Lind Khan fled and his followers scattered.

sentences.zh: 或得俘，言同行凡千餘戶，方苦無所歸，上命英俄爾岱及梅勒額真覺羅布爾吉將二千人往蹟之。

translations.literal: Someone captured a prisoner who said more than a thousand households traveling together were suffering with nowhere to go; the emperor ordered Ying'e'erdai and Meiren Commander Jioro Buerji to lead two thousand men to track them.
translations.idiomatic: Captives reported a thousand homeless households; he and Buerji tracked them with two thousand men.

sentences.zh: 英俄爾岱等行遇蒙古頭人侯痕巴圖魯率千戶將來歸，遣使謁上；

translations.literal: As Ying'e'erdai marched he met Mongol chief Houhen Baturu leading a thousand households about to submit and sent envoys to the emperor;
translations.idiomatic: En route Houhen Baturu with a thousand households sought submission;

sentences.zh: 复遇台吉布顏圖，縱兵擊殺之，斬二百餘，俘四十奔愬於上，言：「我曹自察？

translations.literal: again he met Taiji Buyantu, set troops to attack and kill them, beheaded more than two hundred, captured forty who fled to complain to the emperor, saying: "We had come from Chahar
translations.idiomatic: he attacked Buyantu, killing two hundred; survivors complained they had come from Chahar

sentences.zh: 以還。

translations.literal: to return.
translations.idiomatic: to submit.

sentences.zh: 上以駝馬及所俘，賚英俄爾岱及諸將士。

translations.literal: The emperor bestowed camels, horses, and captives on Ying'e'erdai and the officers and soldiers.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor rewarded him with camels, horses, and captives.

sentences.zh: 既，布顏圖部哈爾來歸，遇大軍，乞降不見允，橫被屠戮。」

translations.literal: Later Buyantu's follower Har submitted; meeting the great army, he begged to surrender but was not granted it and was slaughtered indiscriminately.
translations.idiomatic: Later Har of Buyantu's band submitted but was massacred despite pleading.

sentences.zh: 上怒，命盡奪所賚。

translations.literal: The emperor in anger ordered all rewards confiscated.
translations.idiomatic: Enraged, the emperor stripped every reward.

sentences.zh: 英俄爾岱尋以考滿進三等梅勒章京。

translations.literal: Soon Ying'e'erdai, on completing his term, was promoted to third-rank meiren commander.
translations.idiomatic: Soon a completed term raised him to third-rank meiren commander.

sentences.zh: 十年春，諸貝勒及蒙古諸部以太宗功德日隆，議上尊號，令英俄爾岱齎書使朝鮮喻意​​。

translations.literal: In the spring of the tenth year the princes and Mongol tribes, as Taizong's merit daily grew, deliberated on offering a honorific title and ordered Ying'e'erdai with a letter to go to Korea to explain the intent.
